text: Rotated-hybrid Riemann solver Rotated Riemann methods construct dissipation using directions beyond the face normal. Ren’s rotated Roe method (2003) and Nishikawa–Kitamura’s rotated-hybrid method (2008) are related but distinct. Problem and representative equations For 2D Euler states U_L,U_R and unit face normal n, resolve n into orthogonal unit directions n₁,n₂ with weights αᵢ=n·nᵢ. The formula below defines this atlas’s educational HLLE/Roe experiment, not the optimized dissipation formula in the 2008 paper. n=α1n1+α2n2,F^(n)=α1F^HLLE(n1)+α2F^Roe(n2).n=α1​n1​+α2​n2​,F(n)=α1​FHLLE​(n1​)+α2​FRoe​(n2​). Algorithm The implementation aligns n₁ with the velocity jump, orienting directions to have nonnegative projections on the face normal. A tiny jump falls back to the face tangent. Rotate the same states into each frame, evaluate HLLE/Roe, rotate momentum fluxes back and combine. This differs from a pressure-sensor flux blend. Conditions and pitfalls Roe (1981) supplies the component approximate solver. The 2003 rotated-method paper is by Y.-X. Ren; the 2008 rotated-hybrid paper is by Hiroaki Nishikawa and Keiichi Kitamura. Roe, Nishikawa, Ismail and Scalabrin (2005) is related carbuncle research, not the authorship/date of that 2008 paper. No universal carbuncle or positivity guarantee is claimed here. What to check Check constant states, flux reversal under state/normal exchange and rotational covariance.
